intro: EHN Guardians Atlantic is EHN Canada's inpatient trauma and addiction centre for people who serve: Canadian Armed Forces members, veterans, RCMP, police, firefighters, paramedics, correctional officers, dispatchers and frontline healthcare workers. We listed it for years as the Atlantic Centre for Trauma, when the program ran out of a house in Nictaux in the Annapolis Valley. In May 2026 it reopened in a new, purpose-built building at 610 Myers Point Road in Head of Jeddore, on the Eastern Shore about 45 minutes from Halifax.

Atlantic Centre for Trauma is dedicated to providing addiction and trauma recovery to military members and first responders. They understand that these professions place individuals at a unique risk of experiencing trauma and its effects. Atlantic Centre for Trauma’s inpatient facility, located in beautiful Nova Scotia, provides a peaceful and calming setting for recovery. The facility offers alcohol and drug recovery and care for co-occurring conditions with special tracks for family care and trauma-specific programs. Patients are given a secure, comfortable, and warm environment to help them recover. The campus is surrounded by nature and offers a fully equipped gym, lovely hiking routes, and freshly prepared, regionally inspired meals.

pillars.title: Treatment Opportunities
pillars.body: The Atlantic Centre for Trauma provides a range of therapeutic interventions that address various mental health conditions. Some of these interventions include Cognitive Processing Therapy (CPT), Cognitive Behavioral Therapy (CBT), Dialectical Behavioral Therapy (DBT), Eye Movement Desensitization and Reprocessing (EMDR), and art therapy. These interventions take place in an individual or small-group treatment setting. In addition, the Atlantic Centre for Trauma offers integrated therapies including yoga, meditation, physical exercise, healthy eating, and good sleep habits. The facility also provides specialized treatments such as Repetitive Transcranial Magnetic Stimulation (rTMS) and Ketamine Therapy.

pillars.title: Trauma-specific and Family Program
pillars.body: Atlantic Centre for Trauma offers specialized services to treat PTSD, mood disorders, sexual trauma, and chronic pain, with or without co-occurring substance use disorders. Patients receive a comprehensive treatment program that includes detox, stabilization, psychoeducation, skill-building, and relapse prevention. The facility also offers family programs that aim to educate family members about the patient’s condition, provide them with tools for coping, and encourage healing together.

pillars.title: Aftercare and Alumni Network
pillars.body: Atlantic Centre for Trauma’s aftercare program is designed to provide ongoing support to patients even after they have completed their treatment program. All qualified patients who finish therapy are given one year of aftercare. Additionally, the facility’s lifetime alumni network, Thrive, is available to provide patients with a supportive community of individuals who have completed the same journey towards recovery.

overview: The Atlantic Centre for Trauma is a leading rehab center that offers a peaceful and welcoming environment for individuals struggling with addiction and trauma. Located on the Eastern Shore of Nova Scotia, the center provides a comfortable and secure space for patients to begin their journey towards recovery. With homey bedrooms, delicious homestyle meals made with local ingredients, and inviting common spaces, patients feel like they are part of a supportive community rather than a clinical institution.

In addition to the comfortable accommodations, patients have access to state-of-the-art facilities that promote physical and mental wellness during their recovery. The center offers access to both on-site and off-site gyms, as well as local trails and paths that provide the perfect setting for exercise and meditation. Patients can also enjoy the serene surroundings and find peace and tranquillity to aid in their healing journey. Overall, the Atlantic Centre for Trauma is a great option for those looking for a rehab center that promotes recovery in a safe, welcoming, and supportive environment.

afterOverview: There are three inpatient programs. The 7-week trauma, PTSD and psychological injury program is for people whose main struggle is an operational stress injury. The 9-week trauma, PTSD and addiction program adds detox and relapse prevention for people who also use alcohol or drugs. A third program, at least 28 days long with a cohort of eleven, is for guardians whose main problem is addiction without a current trauma diagnosis.

Most clients do not pay out of pocket. EHN works with Veterans Affairs Canada, Canadian Forces Health Services, RCMP Health Services and workers' compensation boards, and the program pages also mention insurance, union benefits and employer programs. Admissions handles approvals and paperwork, and shares pricing after a free assessment.

location.heading: EHN Guardians Atlantic in Head of Jeddore, Nova Scotia
location.intro: EHN Guardians Atlantic is on Myers Point Road in Head of Jeddore, on the ocean along Nova Scotia's Eastern Shore. Halifax and Halifax Stanfield airport are each about 45 minutes away by car, Dartmouth is a little closer, and Musquodoboit Harbour is about 10 minutes down Highway 7. From Truro the drive is roughly an hour and a half, and from Moncton it takes a bit over three hours.

faqIntro: Answers come from the centre's listing and the EHN Canada website. Still unsure? Call, it's free and confidential.

faqs.q: Is Atlantic Centre for Trauma only for military members and first responders?
faqs.a: Yes. The centre now admits only people who serve: active military, veterans, RCMP, police, firefighters, paramedics, correctional officers, emergency dispatchers, and border and immigration staff. EHN's program pages also include frontline healthcare workers. You can come with or without an addiction.

faqs.q: Is EHN Guardians Atlantic still in Nictaux?
faqs.a: No. The program moved to a new building at 610 Myers Point Road in Head of Jeddore, on the Eastern Shore, which opened in May 2026. EHN's location list now gives only the Head of Jeddore address. EHN's other Nova Scotia centre, EHN Bellwood Nova Scotia in Lawrencetown, is still in the Annapolis Valley.

faqs.q: How long are the programs at EHN Guardians Atlantic?
faqs.a: The trauma, PTSD and psychological injury program runs 7 weeks, and the trauma, PTSD and addiction program runs 9 weeks. The addiction and mental health program has no set end date but lasts at least 28 days. EHN says the care team or your funder can adjust the length.

faqs.q: What is the length of the treatment program?
faqs.a: The length of the treatment program varies depending on the patient’s needs and severity of the condition.

faqs.q: What is the cost of treatment at Atlantic Centre for Trauma?
faqs.a: The cost of treatment varies depending on the level of care required and the length of stay. Insurance coverage may also be applicable.

faqs.q: Can Veterans Affairs, the RCMP or WCB pay for treatment?
faqs.a: Often, yes. EHN names Veterans Affairs Canada, Canadian Forces Health Services, RCMP Health Services and workers' compensation boards as funders, and its program pages add insurance, union benefits and employer programs. Admissions helps with the approvals and paperwork.

faqs.q: Does EHN Guardians Atlantic offer medical detox?
faqs.a: Yes. Medically supervised detox is available when you need it, with 24/7 monitoring. Nurses and counsellors are on site around the clock and doctors are available.

faqs.q: Where is EHN Guardians Atlantic and how do I get there?
faqs.a: The centre is at 610 Myers Point Road in Head of Jeddore, on the Eastern Shore of Nova Scotia. It is about 45 minutes by car from Halifax and from Halifax Stanfield International Airport, and about 10 minutes from Musquodoboit Harbour along Highway 7.

faqs.q: Does Atlantic Centre for Trauma provide outpatient services?
faqs.a: Not as a separate outpatient program. Every program at EHN Guardians Atlantic includes one year of aftercare, with a weekly therapy group alongside other alumni once you finish your inpatient stay, plus lifelong membership in the EHN Canada Alumni Association.

No referral is needed, but you do need to be a military member, veteran or first responder. An admissions coordinator talks with you first to confirm eligibility, and complex cases are reviewed one by one by the clinical team.

The trauma programs use cognitive processing therapy, prolonged exposure (including exposures with occupational therapists), CBT and DBT, with individual and group therapy and psychoeducation. The addiction program adds motivational interviewing, Seeking Safety groups, art and music therapy, yoga and equine-supported work.

faqs.q: Are visitors allowed during the patient's stay?
faqs.a: Yes, visitors are allowed during scheduled visiting hours.

faqs.q: Will family members be involved in the patient's treatment program?
faqs.a: Yes, family members are encouraged to participate in family programs that educate them about the patient’s condition and provide them with tools for coping.
